answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to bond scarce stake that it forfeits on misconduct. Spinning up ten thousand fake identities then costs ten thousand times that bond, so an attacker's capital leaks away like water from a hollow log. The expense of every forged persona climbs the way a vine chokes a neglected fence, strangling the scheme before it spreads. Meanwhile honest agents traverse the economic tundra with low overhead, because each new identity still demands real collateral, making mass forgery unprofitable and self-defeating.
